label: early-prefix trigram: t/d, then o/2/t/r, then consonant (l,w,t,n,f,r,c)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps). 91% of activation mass is in the original phase at positions 2-4 (mostly t=2,3), never at t=0,1 or the delimiter; the rest is weak copy-phase echoes. It fires on a specific 3-token context: two steps back is t or d (sometimes i/o/w), the previous token is o or 2 (also r/t), and the current token is a consonant from {l,w,t,n,f,r,c} (e.g. "t o r", "i t 2 n", "t t n"). The best conjunction reaches only dev F1 ~0.44 (precision ~0.37, recall ~0.55): many matching trigrams stay silent and some activations come from other contexts (e.g. late copy-phase l), so the exact lookup table is not captured. Activations are small and uniform (median 0.11, max 0.20); I did not find a clear magnitude modulator, but top activations do lean toward the prev o/2 + prev2 t/d core. It does not fire on vowels, at the first two positions, or at the delimiter.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & out_tok=i (+5.52), in_tok=l (+4.90), prev_tok=o (+4.74), phase=0 & in_tok=n (+3.93), phase=2 & in_tok=v (+3.93), prev2_tok=t (+3.81). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-3.17), t=7 (-2.89), L=9 & recall_idx=-1 (-2.81), orig8=- (-2.61).
